exactText: I expect it will become nearly impossible by 2030.
sourceQuote: I expect it will become nearly impossible by 2030.
normalizedClaim: By 2030 it will become nearly impossible to devise tests that regular humans can pass but AI cannot.
resolutionCriteria: Difficulty in constructing novel tasks solvable by average humans but unsolvable by frontier AI systems by end of 2030, as assessed by independent researchers.

exactText: I think we’re probably looking at AGI by 2030, early 2030s, most likely.
sourceQuote: I think we’re probably looking at AGI by 2030, early 2030s, most likely.
normalizedClaim: AGI is most likely to arrive around 2030 or the early 2030s.
resolutionCriteria: Consensus achievement of AGI (end of the human-AI gap on novel tasks) by approximately 2035 at latest.
Recognition of AGI (inability to construct differentiating human-AI tests) occurring near 2030.

exactText: My current timeline for when we'll solve ARC-AGI is, "a couple of years". A range of 1 to 3 years.
sourceQuote: My current timeline for when we'll solve ARC-AGI is, "a couple of years". A range of 1 to 3 years.
normalizedClaim: ARC-AGI (original or equivalent) will be solved within 1–3 years from October 2024 (i.e., by ~2027).
resolutionCriteria: Frontier systems achieving human-level or better performance on ARC-AGI-1/2 by end of 2027, per ARC Prize official scores.

exactText: I don't think the rise of AGI will lead to a sudden exponential explosion in AI capabilities.
sourceQuote: I don't think the rise of AGI will lead to a sudden exponential explosion in AI capabilities.
normalizedClaim: Achievement of AGI will not trigger a sudden exponential explosion (intelligence explosion) in AI capabilities.
resolutionCriteria: Absence of discontinuous, self-reinforcing capability jumps immediately following AGI-level systems through 2035.

exactText: the early 2023 narrative that all we needed to solve AGI was scaling up base LLMs did not pan out.
sourceQuote: the early 2023 narrative that all we needed to solve AGI was scaling up base LLMs did not pan out.
normalizedClaim: Pure scaling of base LLMs without additional techniques (test-time compute, harnesses) is insufficient for AGI.
resolutionCriteria: Continued failure of pure base LLM scaling to solve ARC-AGI or achieve fluid intelligence without test-time adaptation by 2028.

exactText: as long as it's easy to come up with tasks that any one of you can do that are easy for humans, but that AI cannot figure out no matter how much compute we throw at it, we don't have an AGI yet.
sourceQuote: as long as it's easy to come up with tasks that any one of you can do that are easy for humans, but that AI cannot figure out no matter how much compute we throw at it, we don't have an AGI yet.
normalizedClaim: AGI has not been achieved while it remains easy to invent tasks solvable by ordinary humans but unsolvable by AI regardless of compute.
resolutionCriteria: Persistence of such differentiating tasks as of 2026–2027 confirming current systems are not AGI.

exactText: The trajectory of AI from <1% to 100% over the course of 6 months shows that the benchmark was able to snapshot the recent rise of agentic capabilities. And that rise has happened faster than most people expected, including us.
sourceQuote: that rise has happened faster than most people expected, including us.
normalizedClaim: The rise of agentic capabilities in 2026 occurred faster than expected by Chollet and most observers.
resolutionCriteria: Documented rapid improvement on ARC-AGI-3 from near-zero to high scores within ~6 months of 2026, matching the described trajectory.

resolution.explanation: Chollet reported the observed trajectory as fact in the same post.

evidence.sourceTitle: François Chollet X post on ARC-AGI-3

exactText: Around that time, we’re going to be releasing maybe ARC-AGI 6 or ARC-AGI 7. That’s probably going to be AGI.
sourceQuote: Around that time, we’re going to be releasing maybe ARC-AGI 6 or ARC-AGI 7. That’s probably going to be AGI.
normalizedClaim: AGI will roughly coincide with the release of ARC-AGI versions 6 or 7 in the early 2030s.
resolutionCriteria: Release of ARC-AGI-6/7 occurring near the time when the human-AI performance gap on novel tasks becomes negligible.

exactText: To this day, current base LLMs (considerably scaled up compared to the models from that time) still do not perform well on something as easy as ARC 1 -- and can't even reliably do simple math operations.
sourceQuote: current base LLMs (considerably scaled up compared to the models from that time) still do not perform well on something as easy as ARC 1
normalizedClaim: Even heavily scaled base LLMs (without test-time compute) continue to underperform on ARC-1 as of mid-2026.
resolutionCriteria: Official ARC Prize leaderboards showing pure base models (no TTC) remaining well below human performance on ARC-AGI-1 in 2026.

resolution.explanation: Stated as contemporaneous observation consistent with public ARC results.
